The petitioners have filed the present petition, inter alia, praying as under:
"(I) Grant DECLARATION and/or appropriate writ, order or direction declaring the impugned acquisition proceedings vis- a-vis Subject Land [i.e. land measuring one bigha (01 bigha) in Kh. no. 29//1 (04-16) in revenue estate of village MUBARAKPUR DABAS, Delhi] stands lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act,
2013."
2.

. The petitioners claim that their share is confined to 1 bigha out of the aforesaid land.

3. It is the petitioners' case that the acquisition of subject land has lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 [2013 Act] as neither the compensation for the subject land has been tendered nor the possession of the same was taken over.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 [2013 Act]
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Insofar as, the petitioners' case that the compensation has not been tendered, the said averment is not controverted by the LAC and despite repeated opportunities, the LAC has not filed any counter-affidavit countering the aforesaid submission.

In the aforesaid view, the petitioners'
contention that the compensation for acquisition of the subject land was not tendered is required to be accepted.
5. The second question required to be considered is whether the possession of the subject land was taken over.
The DDA has filed a counter- affidavit affirming that 4 bighas and 10 biswas of land out of the total land comprising of 4 bighas and 16 biswas was taken over by LAC and handed over to DDA.
The DDA has also filed copy of the possession proceedings to establish the same.
6. The petitioners' contention that the land has not been acquired is based on an information received pursuant to an application filed under the Right to Information Act, 2005.

However in view of the averment made by DDA in the counter-affidavit to the effect that possession of 4 bighas and 10 biswas of land were acquired coupled with the copy of the possession proceedings, we are unable to accept the petitioners' contention that the This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/03/2025 at 21:54:35 possession of 4 bighas and 10 biswas of land out of the subject land was not taken over.
The controversy, that is, confined to remaining 6 biswas of land.
It does appear that the possession of the said 6 biswas of land out of the subject land was not taken over.

7. In the aforesaid context, Mr. Pathak, the learned counsel appearing for LAC submits that majority of the subject land forming part of 29//1 measuring 4 bigha 16 biswas, that is 4 bigha 10 biswas has been taken over, and only 6 biswas remains to be taken over.
He contended that this cannot be construed as a failure on the part of the authorities to take possession due to the land being built up.

He referred to the decision of the Supreme Court in Government of NCT of Delhi & Anr. v.
Dayanand & Anr.: (2023) 5 SCC 381, in support of the said contention.

Government of NCT of Delhi & Anr. v.
Dayanand & Anr.: (2023) 5 SCC 381
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Mr. Nitin Mishra, the learned counsel appearing for DDA, submits that once possession proceedings are drawn in respect of a land, the entire land would be deemed to have been taken over notwithstanding that possession of a part of the land was not taken over.

9. Additionally, the learned counsel for LAC and DDA also contend that the question whether the acquisition has lapsed is no longer res integra as the Supreme Court in the case of Delhi Development Authority v. Fahem Ahmed Khan & Ors., Civil Appeal arising out of SLP(C)

sentences.text: It is stated that Fahem Ahmed Khan owned about 500 Sq. yds (approximately 6 biswas) of the subject land and since the controversy was settled in the case of the petitioner's co-owner, the same would also conclude the dispute in the present petition.
They also point out that the petitioners' case is based on the decision rendered by this court in Fahem Ahmed Khan v. Union of This is a digitally signed order.

10.
This court has reservations as to the proposition that if possession of a part of the land has taken over it would be deemed that the authorities have taken over the possession of entire land.

Prima facie, we are unable to accept that the decision in the case of Government of NCT of Delhi & Anr. v.
Dayanand & Anr. (supra) supports the said contention.

entities.text:
Government of NCT of Delhi & Anr. v.
Dayanand & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case, notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (LA Act) was issued to the concerned land owners inviting them to collect the compensation.

Therefore, in view of the decision in the case of Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal and Ors.: (2020) 8 SCC 129, the court held that acquisition of the land in question had not lapsed by virtue of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal and Ors.: (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. In Government of NCT of Delhi & Anr. v. Dayanand & Anr. (supra) the Supreme Court did record that the major portion of the land in question measuring 19 biswas out of 20 biswas was taken over and only 1 biswas was left out.

entities.text: Government of NCT of Delhi & Anr. v. Dayanand & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, it does not appear that any finding was returned to the effect that the same would constitute taking over of the possession of the entire land.

Paragraph 6 of the said decision, which is relied upon by the respondents is set out below:
"6. Applying the law laid down by this Court in Indore Development Authority [Indore Development Authority (Lapse-5 J.) v. Manoharlal, (2020) 8 SCC 129 :
(2020) 4 SCC (Civ) 496] and considering the facts narrated hereinabove and more particularly, when the major portion of the land in question was taken as far back as on 13-4-2009 by drawing possession proceedings which is held to be permissible in Indore Development Authority

passed by the High Court declaring that the acquisition in respect of land in question is deemed to have lapsed is unsustainable."

sentences.text:
The aforesaid passage does indicate that the Supreme Court decision was based not only on the fact that possession of the majority land was taken over but that a notice under Section 12(2) of the LA Act was also served on the original writ petitioner and he did not collect the compensation offered.
13.

Insofar as the decision of the Supreme Court in Delhi Development Authority v Fahem Ahmed Khan & Ors. (supra) is concerned, the learned counsel for the petitioners requests for some time to obtain a clarification.

entities.text: Delhi Development Authority v Fahem Ahmed Khan & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that the said decision was rendered on the basis that there was no dispute that physical possession of Khasra no. 29//1 (04-16) had been taken over by the acquiring authority and handed over to the DDA on 04.04.2006.
The Supreme Court had proceeded on the basis of the facts as recorded in paragraph 11 of the judgment dated 20.03.2018 passed by this court in W.P.(C) 4529/2016.
This is evident from the following extracts of the order passed by the Supreme Court in Delhi Development Authority v Fahem Ahmed Khan & Ors.

entities.text: Delhi Development Authority v Fahem Ahmed Khan & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (supra):

"In the present case, the High Court has clearly noted in paragraph 11 of the impugned judgment that actual physical possession of Khasra No.29/1 (4-16) had been taken by the acquiring authority and handed over to the Delhi This is a digitally signed order.

However,
the Court allowed the writ petition on the finding that the compensation amount has not been paid to the writ petitioner.
We must place on record the stand of the respondent- authority before the High Court on affidavit.
It was stated that the compensation was offered vide Cheque No.075564 dated 16.12.2005.

It is not necessary to dilate on this aspect as the fact that possession had been taken over by the authority in the present case is indisputable."
14.

He submits that paragraph 11 of this court's judgment dated 20.03.2018 did not record that the physical possession of the entire land was taken over but it clearly recorded that only 4 bigha and 10 biswas of the subject land was taken over.
Paragraph 11 of the said decision dated 20.03.2018, which was the subject matter of appeal in Delhi Development Authority v Fahem Ahmed Khan & Ors.

"11. Having regard to the submissions made and the categorical assertion made in the counter affidavit filed by LAC as well as DDA, it is clear that that out of the total land comprised in Khasra No.29//1(4-16), the actual physical possession of only 4 Bighas 10 Biswas of the subject land has been taken and handed over to DDA on 04.04.2006.

However, the compensation thereof has not been paid to the petitioner and since the award having been announced more than five years prior to the commencement of the 2013 Act, the petitioner is entitled to a declaration that the Pavitra Kumar & Anr vs Land Acquisition Collector, North West ...
